links.citation: Thurston Moore has said he met his scene in a record shop while hunting for Velvet Underground records.
Lee Ranaldo, Wikipedia/Sonic Youth -- SST-label admiration rather than a direct sound-influence claim, flagged weaker-tier.
Thurston Moore told Rolling Stone that seeing Glenn Branca play guitars tuned outside of standard tunings "really is what informed a lot of what happened in Sonic Youth."

Thurston Moore has described seeing the Patti Smith Group live as a teenager as the moment he'd been waiting for, and singled out one of her less verse-chorus, almost-improvised songs as directly formative to Sonic Youth's own break from traditional song structure.
Kevin Shields has called the Cocteau Twins/JAMC comparison "garbage," but concedes Psychocandy as "the shared record" between the two bands' sounds.
NME's "Roots of MBV": hearing the Ramones was when Shields realised the guitar could be more than a melodic cosh -- in his words, "a noise generator."
Kevin Shields to Karen Leng, Double J / ABC (8 Apr 2021), on the dark post-punk bands the band drew from: "the best of all was Siouxsie and the Banshees, the Cure and Killing Joke."
Kevin Shields to Karen Leng, Double J / ABC (8 Apr 2021), same answer: "the best of all was Siouxsie and the Banshees, the Cure and Killing Joke."
NPR: Siouxsie Sioux grew up on Bowie and Lou Reed. AllMusic's prose bio recounts her head being turned seeing Bowie perform on television.
Robin Guthrie's page on the band's own site names Siouxsie and the Banshees among the artists who made the beautiful noise that drew a teenage Fraser and Guthrie together.
Guthrie's page on the band's own site: an alienated teenager who loved the Sex Pistols, the Birthday Party, and Siouxsie and the Banshees.
Robin Guthrie, on the band's own site: they were "influenced by guitarists who made a beautiful noise, like Roland S. Howard... it's because of them that we sent a demo to 4AD."
Iggy Pop: "David had said something in Melody Maker about his favorite songs, and he said he liked the Stooges" -- 1971, before the two men had met.
Hook, in Jon Savage's oral history: "Ian was much better educated for things like Can, Kraftwerk, Velvet Underground."

Neil Young has described first hearing Bob Dylan in Winnipeg around 1963, the same year he named Dylan directly in his own lyric on "Flags of Freedom."
Guy Picciotto, Cultural Glitch (Nov 3, 2011): "Fugazi's influences include Bad Brains, the Faith, Void, Minutemen, Black Flag, Sonic Youth, the Ex."

Robert Smith, in Mark Paytress's Siouxsie & the Banshees: The Authorised Biography (2003), p.96, on playing with the Banshees: "On stage that first night with the Banshees, I was blown away by how powerful I felt playing that kind of music. It was so different to what we were doing with the Cure... Being a Banshee really changed my attitude to what I was doing."

Robert Smith named Nick Drake among his five favorite songs for the BBC, saying it embodied "everything I would aspire to in understated mood songwriting," and told Clash that Drake's "Time Has Told Me" gave the band its name.
Smith's BBC five-songs list: "Anarchy in the UK" was "the last time something really major happened to me and changed me."
Smith, Rolling Stone Q&A: "when I first saw the Stranglers, I thought, 'This is it.' And I saw the Buzzcocks the following week, and I thought, 'This is definitely it.'"
Smith, in the Bambarger interview: "When I first got hold of Mogwai's Young Team album, I played it endlessly" -- audible, he has said, on Bloodflowers.
